I couldn't research Psalm 43, so I have no notes for you yet.

The first time I tried to fetch the source pages, the system said I had no more search or fetch uses left for this turn. No pages loaded, so I haven't read Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, New Advent or any other approved site. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Without any pages, that means I can't give you any verse-by-verse notes, comparisons between traditions or other views right now.

If you ask again in a new message, I can do the research. Here are the pages I planned to read first:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:**
  - Enduring Word: enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-43/
  - Bible Hub, one page per verse, which gathers Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes and others: biblehub.com/commentaries/psalms/43-1.htm through 43-5.htm
  - Precept Austin's Psalm 43 page
  - Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on StudyLight or Spurgeon.org
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Gill as the Baptist voice, Matthew Henry, and any Lutheran or Reformed pieces on lament and "hope in God" in vv. 2 and 5.
- **Other views:**
  - NET Bible notes on the textual and wording questions, such as whether Psalms 42 and 43 were first one psalm.
  - Augustine's exposition on New Advent. Older Catholic Bibles number this psalm 42, so I'd look under that number.
  - Catholic.com material on v. 4, "I will go to the altar of God." Whether these pages actually discuss that verse is something I'd need to check, not assume.
